sentences.text: The bus was full by the second stop, and the aisle had become narrow.
A rider stood near the front, arms wrapped around a heavy box.
The box bumped a pole every time the bus slowed down.
A seated rider had a bag taking up the empty half of the next seat.
At first that rider looked out the window and did not move.
Then the rider looked at the box, lifted the bag onto a lap, and nodded.
The standing person sat down at once and said thank you.
Nothing about the bus route changed except one small space.
The box rested on the floor instead of swinging in the aisle.
At the next stop, the two riders did not trade stories or become a pair of friends.
They simply rode more comfortably, and the aisle was clearer.
Making room had taken only a moment, but it fixed a problem everyone nearby could see.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A small kindness that makes room on a crowded bus
A bus route that is changed forever
A heavy box that drives the bus
Two riders who plan a long trip together

questions.explanation: The bus stays full, but one rider moves a bag so another person can sit. That small kindness is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What is the standing person holding?
questions.explanation: The story says a rider stood near the front with arms around a heavy box. The bag belongs to the seated rider.

questions.prompt: The aisle had become narrow. What does narrow mean here?
questions.explanation: Narrow means not wide. The bus is full and the aisle has little space, which is why the box keeps bumping a pole.

questions.prompt: Why does lifting the bag matter to more people than just one rider?

choices.text: It makes the bus skip the next stop
It turns the bag into a ticket
It tells the driver to end the route
It opens a seat and keeps the heavy box out of the aisle

questions.explanation: The story shows the box bumping a pole, then resting on the floor after the seat opens. A reader can figure out that the aisle becomes safer for everyone nearby.
